```{=html}
    <h1>Relic neutrinos</h1>
  </header>
```

::: {.qft-exam-body}
According to the modern cosmological model of the birth and evolution of the Universe, we are surrounded by the so-called *relic neutrinos*. Their temperature today is $T_\nu\approx 1.95$ K ($kT_\nu\approx 1.7\cdot 10^{-4}$ eV), which makes them very hard to observe. Nevertheless, let us think of something. A Nobel Prize is guaranteed!

\(i\) Compute the cross section of the reaction $\nu_e +n\to p+e^-$ at the energy of a relic neutrino. Compute the mass of free neutrons needed to detect 100 such events per year. Do we have a suitable source of free neutrons of the required mass?

If not, suggest an atomic nucleus that could be used instead of free neutrons.

\(ii\) Consider another project: a particle accelerator. If an electron or a muon is accelerated in it to a high enough energy, the lepton can disappear after interacting with a relic antineutrino, producing a pion: $\bar{\nu}_\ell  +\ell^-\to \pi^-$.

a\) Compute the lepton energy needed for this reaction to occur.

b\) Compute the corresponding cross section.

c\) Estimate the luminosity of the accelerator needed to detect a statistically significant number of pions.

\(iii\) Is there a hidden Glashow resonance in the reaction $\bar{\nu}_\ell  +\ell^-\to \pi^-$? (Discuss this idea with the colleague working on that project.) What could follow from it?

\(iv\) Propose your own idea for detecting relic neutrinos and support it with calculations.

:::
